subject: Amplitude scale and strange oscillo() plots

messages.author: 28340b93677bbe7d
messages.subject: Amplitude scale and strange oscillo() plots
parts:
Hi all,

I've just discovered seewave today. I'm a phonetics student trying to find cleaner looking plots for spectrograms/waveforms than what Praat offers. I really like the oscillo() function except it's acting quite strange. The first question is, I'm not quite sure how to specify dB labels on the y-axis - can someone clarify this for me?

The second question is the strange-acting part. When I call oscillo(ake,from=0.82,to=.84), nothing happens in the plot window. I have to call it twice before the plot does anything. If I call it again, the plot window goes blank and only after a 2nd call, does anything show. But the first and third time I call it (as well as the 2nd and 4th "working" times) there's the strange looking squished plot on the sideline (image attached).

I'm running R 3.0.2 with RStudio 0.98.484 on Mavericks 10.9.1.

Thanks!
Nay

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Amplitude scale and strange oscillo() plots
parts: Le 20/12/2013 13:27, Nay San a écrit :

Hi all,

I've just discovered seewave today. I'm a phonetics student trying to find cleaner looking plots for spectrograms/waveforms than what Praat offers. I really like the oscillo() function except it's acting quite strange. The first question is, I'm not quite sure how to specify dB labels on the y-axis - can someone clarify this for me?
The y axis of the oscillo refers to a relative scale "normalised" between -1 and 1, withtout unit. Oscillogram are very rarely ploted on a dB scale (relative or absolute).

The second question is the strange-acting part. When I call oscillo(ake,from=0.82,to=.84), nothing happens in the plot window. I have to call it twice before the plot does anything. If I call it again, the plot window goes blank and only after a 2nd call, does anything show. But the first and third time I call it (as well as the 2nd and 4th "working" times) there's the strange looking squished plot on the sideline (image attached).

This is because you probably plotted a spectrogram before and I could not find a nice way to clean up the layout of the graphical window after a spectrogram plot. You need to close the window (dev.off()).
Jerome

I'm running R 3.0.2 with RStudio 0.98.484 on Mavericks 10.9.1.

Thanks!
Nay

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Amplitude scale and strange oscillo() plots
parts:
I am not sure to understand what you mean by spectral slices.
Now you can add vertical bars and legends manually to any plot with abline() and text(), but this not specific to seewave.
There is also a seewave function to look for local maximum of spectral sections, see localpeaks().
Jerome

messages.author: e14cfb57d640984d
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Amplitude scale and strange oscillo() plots
parts:
Hi Nay,

I believe that what you're looking for may be the spec() function. e.g.

data(sheep)
spec(sheep)

It computes and plots the frequency spectrum for an entire sound. If you're looking to slice a longer sound in to pieces you could do that with the "from" and "to" arguments to spec(), or using cutw().

best,
jesse
